title: Cave of the Hands painted
description: Hunter-gatherers created the famous Cueva de las Manos rock art in Patagonia, with stenciled handprints dated to roughly 7000 BCE.

title: First founding of Buenos Aires
description: Spanish conquistador Pedro de Mendoza established the first settlement at Buenos Aires, which was later abandoned and refounded in 1580.

title: May Revolution
description: The May Revolution in Buenos Aires deposed the Spanish viceroy and created the first local governing junta, beginning Argentina's independence process.

title: Declaration of Independence
description: The Congress of Tucumán formally declared the independence of the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata from Spain.

title: Constitution of Argentina adopted
description: Argentina adopted its national constitution, establishing a federal republic that, with amendments, remains in force today.

title: Women win the right to vote
description: Under the influence of Eva Perón, Argentina enacted female suffrage, allowing women to vote in national elections from 1951.

title: Argentina wins the FIFA World Cup
description: Led by Diego Maradona, Argentina won the football World Cup in Mexico, a defining moment of national pride.

title: Return to democracy
description: Raúl Alfonsín was elected president, ending the military dictatorship and beginning Argentina's modern democratic era.

title: Rise of the Chiripa culture
description: Early agricultural societies developed around Lake Titicaca, laying the foundation for later Andean civilizations in the Bolivian highlands.

title: Tiwanaku civilization flourishes
description: The Tiwanaku state near Lake Titicaca became a major Andean political and religious center, famed for monumental stone architecture.

title: Silver discovered at Potosí
description: Spanish colonists found vast silver deposits at Cerro Rico in Potosí, which became one of the world's largest sources of silver.

title: Bolivia declares independence
description: Bolivia declared independence from Spain, taking its name in honor of liberator Simón Bolívar.

title: War of the Pacific begins
description: Bolivia entered the War of the Pacific against Chile and ultimately lost its coastal territory, becoming landlocked.

title: National Revolution
description: The Bolivian National Revolution brought universal suffrage, land reform, and the nationalization of major tin mines.

title: Evo Morales inaugurated
description: Evo Morales became Bolivia's first indigenous president, leading major constitutional and social reforms.

title: Early settlement at Serra da Capivara
description: Ancient peoples lived in what is now Piauí, leaving extensive rock paintings that are among the oldest evidence of humans in the Americas.

title: Portuguese arrival
description: Pedro Álvares Cabral landed on the Brazilian coast and claimed the territory for Portugal, beginning European colonization.

title: Independence from Portugal
description: Prince Pedro declared Brazil's independence, establishing the Empire of Brazil with himself as Emperor Pedro I.

title: Abolition of slavery
description: Princess Isabel signed the Lei Áurea (Golden Law), abolishing slavery in Brazil, the last country in the Americas to do so.

title: Proclamation of the Republic
description: A military coup overthrew the monarchy and established the First Brazilian Republic, ending the imperial era.

title: Brasília becomes the capital
description: The purpose-built modernist city of Brasília, designed by Oscar Niemeyer and Lúcio Costa, was inaugurated as the new capital.

title: Return to civilian rule
description: Brazil ended over two decades of military dictatorship with a transition to civilian democratic government.

title: Third World Cup title
description: Brazil won its third FIFA World Cup in Mexico, led by Pelé, earning permanent possession of the Jules Rimet Trophy.

title: Monte Verde settlement
description: The Monte Verde site in southern Chile provides some of the earliest evidence of human habitation in the Americas.

title: Magellan sails the strait
description: Ferdinand Magellan navigated the strait at the southern tip of South America that now bears his name, linking the Atlantic and Pacific.

title: Chile declares independence
description: Chile formally declared independence from Spain after victory at the Battle of Maipú, led by Bernardo O'Higgins and José de San Martín.

title: War of the Pacific
description: Chile fought Bolivia and Peru in the War of the Pacific, gaining mineral-rich northern territories.

title: Salvador Allende elected
description: Salvador Allende became the first Marxist elected president in Latin America through open democratic elections.

title: Military coup
description: A coup led by Augusto Pinochet overthrew Allende, beginning a 17-year military dictatorship.

title: Return to democracy
description: Chile transitioned back to civilian democratic rule with the inauguration of President Patricio Aylwin.

title: Rescue of 33 trapped miners
description: Thirty-three miners trapped underground for 69 days at the San José mine were rescued in an operation watched worldwide.

title: Early goldworking cultures
description: Indigenous peoples in present-day Colombia began producing sophisticated gold artifacts, later inspiring the El Dorado legend.

title: Founding of Santa Marta
description: Spanish settlers founded Santa Marta, one of the oldest surviving European cities in South America.

title: Cry of Independence
description: The events of July 20 in Bogotá marked the start of Colombia's struggle for independence from Spain.

title: Battle of Boyacá
description: Simón Bolívar's decisive victory at Boyacá secured the independence of New Granada and the founding of Gran Colombia.

title: Separation of Panama
description: Panama seceded from Colombia with U.S. support, leading to the construction of the Panama Canal.

title: Bogotazo riots
description: The assassination of leader Jorge Eliécer Gaitán sparked deadly riots in Bogotá and ushered in the period known as La Violencia.

title: García Márquez wins Nobel Prize
description: Colombian author Gabriel García Márquez received the Nobel Prize in Literature, celebrated for magical realism.

title: Peace deal with the FARC
description: The Colombian government signed a historic peace accord with the FARC guerrillas, ending decades of armed conflict.

title: Valdivia culture pottery
description: The Valdivia culture on Ecuador's coast produced some of the oldest known ceramics in the Americas.

title: Inca conquest of the highlands
description: The Inca Empire expanded into the Andean highlands of present-day Ecuador, making Quito a major regional center.

title: Spanish found Quito
description: Spanish conquistadors established the city of Quito on the site of an Inca settlement after the conquest.

title: Battle of Pichincha
description: Antonio José de Sucre's victory at Pichincha secured Ecuador's independence from Spanish rule.

title: Ecuador becomes a republic
description: Ecuador separated from Gran Colombia and established itself as an independent sovereign republic.

title: Darwin visits the Galápagos
description: Charles Darwin studied the unique wildlife of the Galápagos Islands, observations that informed his theory of evolution.

title: Adoption of the US dollar
description: Facing severe economic crisis, Ecuador abandoned the sucre and adopted the U.S. dollar as its official currency.

title: Rights of Nature constitution
description: Ecuador adopted a new constitution that became the first in the world to recognize legally enforceable rights of nature.

title: First Dutch settlement
description: The Dutch established trading posts along the Essequibo River, beginning sustained European colonization of the region.

title: Berbice slave rebellion
description: Enslaved Africans led by Cuffy staged a major uprising in the Dutch colony of Berbice, a landmark in resistance to slavery.

title: British take control
description: Britain formally acquired the colonies of Essequibo, Demerara, and Berbice, later unified as British Guiana in 1831.

title: Indentured laborers arrive
description: After slavery's abolition, indentured workers from India began arriving, reshaping Guyana's population and culture.

title: Independence from Britain
description: Guyana gained independence from the United Kingdom, becoming a sovereign nation within the Commonwealth.

title: Cooperative Republic declared
description: Guyana became a republic, severing remaining constitutional ties to the British monarchy.

title: Major offshore oil discovery
description: ExxonMobil announced a large oil discovery offshore, transforming Guyana into one of the world's fastest-growing economies.

title: Founding of Asunción
description: Spanish explorers founded Asunción, which became a key base for colonization of the Río de la Plata region.

title: Jesuit missions established
description: Jesuits founded reductions among the Guaraní people, creating communities that blended Christian and indigenous life.

title: Paraguay declares independence
description: Paraguay declared its independence from Spain, becoming one of the first South American nations to break free.

title: War of the Triple Alliance begins
description: Paraguay entered a devastating war against Brazil, Argentina, and Uruguay that decimated its population.

title: Chaco War with Bolivia
description: Paraguay fought Bolivia over the Gran Chaco region, ultimately securing most of the disputed territory.

title: End of Stroessner dictatorship
description: A coup ended Alfredo Stroessner's 35-year rule, opening the way for democratic government in Paraguay.

title: Guaraní recognized officially
description: A new constitution made Guaraní an official language alongside Spanish, reflecting the nation's bilingual identity.

title: Caral, oldest city in the Americas
description: The city of Caral in the Supe Valley arose as one of the oldest urban centers in the Americas, with monumental pyramids.

title: Machu Picchu built
description: The Inca constructed the mountain citadel of Machu Picchu during the reign of Pachacuti at the height of their empire.

title: Spanish capture Atahualpa
description: Francisco Pizarro captured the Inca emperor Atahualpa at Cajamarca, leading to the fall of the Inca Empire.

title: Founding of Lima
description: Pizarro founded Lima, which became the capital of the Spanish Viceroyalty of Peru and a center of colonial power.

title: Peru declares independence
description: José de San Martín proclaimed Peru's independence from Spain in Lima, a key step in liberating South America.

title: Battle of Ayacucho
description: Patriot forces under Sucre defeated the Spanish royalist army at Ayacucho, securing independence across the continent.

title: Machu Picchu brought to global attention
description: Explorer Hiram Bingham publicized Machu Picchu to the wider world, making it an international symbol of the Inca.

title: Fall of the Fujimori government
description: President Alberto Fujimori's authoritarian government collapsed amid corruption scandals, restoring democratic transition.

title: Early English settlement
description: English colonists established plantations along the Suriname River, beginning sustained European settlement.

title: Dutch acquire Suriname
description: Under the Treaty of Breda, the Dutch gained Suriname from England in exchange for New Amsterdam (New York).

title: Maroon peace treaties
description: Escaped enslaved Africans known as Maroons secured treaties with the Dutch recognizing their autonomous communities.

title: Abolition of slavery
description: The Netherlands abolished slavery in Suriname, after which indentured laborers were recruited from Asia.

title: Independence from the Netherlands
description: Suriname gained full independence from the Netherlands, becoming a sovereign republic.

title: Military coup
description: A military coup led by Dési Bouterse overthrew the government, beginning years of military-dominated rule.

title: New democratic constitution
description: Suriname adopted a new constitution and held elections, restoring civilian democratic government.

title: Founding of Montevideo
description: The Spanish founded Montevideo as a military stronghold to counter Portuguese expansion in the region.

title: Artigas leads independence movement
description: José Gervasio Artigas led the struggle for autonomy, becoming the revered national hero of Uruguay.

title: Independence recognized
description: The Treaty of Montevideo established Uruguay as an independent buffer state between Argentina and Brazil.

title: Batlle y Ordóñez reforms
description: President José Batlle y Ordóñez launched progressive reforms that made Uruguay one of the most advanced welfare states.

title: First FIFA World Cup hosted and won
description: Uruguay hosted and won the inaugural FIFA World Cup, defeating Argentina in the final in Montevideo.

title: Return to democracy
description: Uruguay returned to civilian democratic rule after years of military dictatorship.

title: Legalization of cannabis
description: Uruguay became the first country in the world to fully legalize and regulate the cannabis market.

title: Columbus reaches the coast
description: On his third voyage, Christopher Columbus became the first European to reach the coast of present-day Venezuela.

title: Founding of Caracas
description: Spanish colonists founded Santiago de León de Caracas, which grew into Venezuela's capital city.

title: Venezuela declares independence
description: Venezuela became the first Spanish American colony to formally declare its independence from Spain.

title: Battle of Carabobo
description: Simón Bolívar's victory at Carabobo effectively secured Venezuelan independence from Spanish rule.

title: Separation from Gran Colombia
description: Venezuela seceded from Gran Colombia to become a fully independent sovereign republic.

title: Start of the oil era
description: Commercial oil production began, transforming Venezuela into one of the world's leading petroleum exporters.

title: Co-founder of OPEC
description: Venezuela helped found the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries to coordinate oil policy.

title: Hugo Chávez becomes president
description: Hugo Chávez took office and launched the Bolivarian Revolution, reshaping Venezuela's politics and economy.
